protections: matchFileSnapshot confines the caller-supplied filePath to the project root before any filesystem access, covering the create branch (mkdir + write), the overwrite branch (write) and the read/compare branch; no such decision exists anywhere at the pinned commit (src/assertions/snapshots.ts:732-768).

SnapshotEnvironment file I/O stays inside the directory the environment was configured with, so a snapshot filepath cannot escape the snapshot tree: saveSnapshotFile writes (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:65-69), removeSnapshotFile unlinks (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:80-86) and prepareDirectory mkdirs (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:88-92) with no root check, while the only configurable directory is snapshotDir (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:44-47), which resolveSnapshotPath deliberately allows to be absolute (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:71-78).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The published advisory is arbitrary file write, not read; this branch only reads the outside file and folds its content into the mismatch error (src/assertions/snapshots.ts:764-768), so a guard placed on the write paths (src/assertions/snapshots.ts:740-744, 760) is argued to be sufficient.

The in-repo precedent only resolves absolute paths and compares strings (src/coverage/filter.ts:85-90), and the published check is described as resolving against a root and prefix-checking it, so a lexical and absolute-only guard is argued to be exactly what the fix requires; relative traversal, a root equal to the path itself, a non-existent nested target and a symlinked root are treated as refinements.

The documented entry point is the matcher (docs/api/assertions.md:450-456) and matchFileSnapshot is treated as an internal helper, so guarding the expect() wrapper is argued to cover the advisory route.

An absolute snapshotDir is a supported, tested configuration (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:73-75; tests/unit/snapshot-improvements.test.ts:348-353) and the filepath comes from the runner's test-file list rather than from the snapshot assertion argument the advisory names, while the class is not exported from the package (package.json:11-16, src/index.ts:22), so confinement is argued to belong only to matchFileSnapshot.
The advisory is arbitrary file write, not deletion, and cleanup only removes paths the runner itself resolved (src/assertions/snapshot-manager.ts:84), so unlink is argued to be out of scope.

The path is manufactured internally by a stack walk that keeps __snapshots__ next to the declaring test file (src/assertions/snapshots.ts:442-469), so there is no caller-supplied value to traverse with; the only fallback is process.cwd() (src/assertions/snapshots.ts:468).

prepareDirectory is a low-level helper invoked with the dirname of a target path (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:66-68), and a direct call is already equivalent to the caller running mkdir itself.

Writing a coverage report to a caller-configured reportsDirectory is the documented feature itself (src/coverage/index.ts:444), a different module family from the snapshot writer the advisory names, and the reporter classes are constructed only from that config.

masking: Once a lexical or absolute-only prefix check is in place at src/assertions/snapshots.ts:732, the remaining escape is a link inside the root that points outside it, so the symlink shape (T3) only becomes visible after the plain traversal shapes are rejected.

conflicts.what: Rooting every snapshot write at process.cwd() contradicts the absolute and tmpdir snapshot paths the environment must keep writing: tests/unit/snapshot-matchers.test.ts:33-95, tests/unit/snapshot-client.test.ts:188-196 and tests/unit/snapshot-improvements.test.ts:372-387 all pass absolute paths outside the repository, so the saveSnapshotFile guard has to key off the environment's own snapshotDir (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:44-47, 71-78) rather than cwd.

A realpath-based confinement, needed to close the symlinked-root shape, breaks legitimate symlinked roots (a tmpdir root reached through a link), while a lexical prefix compare leaves that shape open; one guard has to satisfy both the strict and the permissive requirement.

Confining removeSnapshotFile before unlink breaks the obsolete-cleanup contract when resolveSnapshotPath is supplied by the environment (tests/unit/snapshot-client.test.ts:294-322 returns a path outside any test-file directory), so the delete-side guard must be scoped to the same configured directory as the write-side guard rather than to the test file's location.

fairness_risks: The pinned file-snapshot tests call matchFileSnapshot with os.tmpdir() paths and no root (tests/unit/snapshot-matchers.test.ts:33-42, 57-69, 85-95); a check rooted at cwd rejects them, so the reference fix has to take or resolve a root argument. Hidden tests that assume a root parameter or a particular position for it make the task depend on an API shape the report never names.

Absolute snapshot paths are a supported, tested use (tests/unit/snapshot-matchers.test.ts:33-42; tests/unit/snapshot-client.test.ts:188-196; tests/unit/snapshot-improvements.test.ts:348-353), so a rule that refuses every absolute path contradicts a legitimate, documented use.

SnapshotClient, SnapshotManager and NodeSnapshotEnvironment are documented as snapshot API (docs/architecture.md:92-93) but are exported from neither the package (package.json:11-16 has a single '.' export) nor src/index.ts:22, and no src module imports them; a solver can therefore argue T5/T6/T8 are unreachable, which is exactly the dismissal attached to them.

The default `new NodeSnapshotEnvironment()` uses a relative '__snapshots__' (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:44-47), so a confinement that keys off an absolute snapshotDir leaves the default configuration unprotected; the alternative, a cwd-rooted default, breaks the pinned tmpdir tests. Any hidden test here has to pick one and say which.

Coverage reporting legitimately writes to a caller-configured reportsDirectory (src/coverage/reporters/json.ts:35-40, src/coverage/reporters/lcov.ts:115-117, default './coverage' at src/coverage/index.ts:444), so a blanket 'no caller path outside cwd' rule contradicts a documented feature.

The repository's own path-confinement idiom, allowExternal (src/coverage/filter.ts:84-90), only resolves when nodePath.isAbsolute(filePath), so copying it verbatim into the snapshot guard leaves relative '..' traversal open; the tempting in-repo precedent is itself the wrong shape, and a benchmark that mirrors it would be self-contradictory.

matchSnapshot writes next to the declaring test file (src/assertions/snapshots.ts:442-469); for a consumer whose tests live outside the project root, confining it would break legitimate use, and refusing that shape protects nothing because there is no caller-supplied argument.

design.why: One well-written guard at the top of matchFileSnapshot (T1) is a single decision but carries three distinct misjudgements: a write-only guard leaves the read/compare branch (T2) returning arbitrary file content in the mismatch error, and a lexical or absolute-only check copied from src/coverage/filter.ts:85-90 leaves relative traversal, the root-equals-root case, non-existent nested targets and a symlinked root (T3) open. The other two groups are separate implementations that need their own confinement and each has a different, strong reason to dismiss: saveSnapshotFile reached through SnapshotClient.loadSnapshots (T5; a supported absolute snapshotDir, no package export) and removeSnapshotFile reached through SnapshotManager.cleanup (T6; deletion rather than write, runner-resolved paths). That mix beats a single-site task because T2 is the absent-protection-plus-dismissal route DeepSeek misses, T3 (and T5's requirement to keep an absolute snapshotDir working) is the over-hardening route MiMo misses, and the three dismissals are genuinely different rather than the same 'the report did not name it' argument repeated. T5/T6 can be scoped to the existing absolute snapshotDir knob (src/assertions/snapshot-environment.ts:44-47, 73-75) so the pinned tmpdir tests stay green; the matchFileSnapshot default root remains the fairness issue noted above and has to be settled by the task author. T7, T8 and T9 are deliberately excluded: T7 has no caller-supplied value, T8 only creates directories, and T9 is a different configured-output feature.
